title: What rule is hiding in each of these three rows of numbers?
description: Farhan finds chalk rows of numbers on his courtyard floor with some numbers rubbed out. The video finds the rule of each row and fills the blanks.
teaching_notes: One idea: take two neighbours, find the gap, and use the whole gap as the rule. Watch for children who read one digit only, or use two numbers with a blank between them.

source: Let Us Do 1 (a), (b), (c), continue the patterns
video_script.why: The child can find the rule of a short row and now meets rows with a blank in the middle and rows whose rule is not a round number.
video_script.substitution: Take two numbers that sit side by side, find the whole gap, test it on the next pair, and use it to fill the blanks.
video_script.anchor: chalk rows of numbers on Farhan's courtyard floor, with some numbers rubbed out by rain
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu reads only the thousands digit of the third row, five then six then seven, and says the rule is add one thousand. The whole numbers change by less than that.
video_script.payoff_line: the rule is add one hundred eleven

final_answer.spoken: add one hundred eleven, add one thousand fifty, add nine hundred

never_show: the answer rows before the idea part
maths_rules: slip: add 1,000 would give 5,501 + 1,000 = 6,501, but the row has 6,401
a blank hides a step, so the gap must come from two numbers that sit side by side
video_script.design: Exercise: find the rule of three rows. Hint: use two neighbours. Three chalk rows sit on the stage; the gaps arrive as labels in the idea part.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='story'/>Farhan writes rows of numbers with chalk on his courtyard floor. The rain has rubbed out some of them.
<bookmark mark='one'/>The first row goes four hundred fifty six, five hundred sixty seven and six hundred seventy eight.
<bookmark mark='two'/>The second row starts with one thousand fifty and then has a blank. After it come three thousand one hundred fifty and four thousand two hundred.
<bookmark mark='three'/>The third row starts with five thousand five hundred one. Then come six thousand four hundred one and seven thousand three hundred one.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Continue each row by filling the blanks.

marks.stop: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

narration: <bookmark mark='pair'/>Pick two numbers that sit side by side, and take away the smaller from the larger.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>If the gap is the same each time, that gap is the rule.
<bookmark mark='blank'/>Never use two numbers that have a blank between them.
<bookmark mark='try'/>Use the rule to fill each blank. Try again with this.

beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows add 1,000 beside the third row; the thousands digits 5, 6, 7 are circled; the whole numbers 5,501 and 6,401 are shown; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.digit: the thousands digits are circled and the whole numbers 5,501 and 6,401 appear beside them
marks.strike: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>In the third row, the thousands digit goes five, six, seven, so the rule is add one thousand.
<bookmark mark='digit'/>That looks at one digit only. The whole number must change by the same amount each time.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Check the full gap, not one digit.

beats.on_screen: the first row gets its gap label +111; the board reads 567 − 456 = 111; the blanks fill with 789, 900, 1,011, 1,122

marks.fill: the other three blanks fill with 900, 1,011, 1,122

narration: <bookmark mark='gap'/>In the first row, five hundred sixty seven take away four hundred fifty six leaves one hundred eleven.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The next gap is the same, so the rule is add one hundred eleven.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Add one hundred eleven to six hundred seventy eight to get seven hundred eighty nine.
<bookmark mark='fill'/>Keep adding to reach nine hundred, one thousand eleven and one thousand one hundred twenty two.

beats.on_screen: the second row gets the board line 4,200 − 3,150 = 1,050; the blank fills with 2,100; the check line 2,100 + 1,050 = 3,150 appears
narration: <bookmark mark='side'/>In the second row, use the two numbers that sit side by side.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>Four thousand two hundred take away three thousand one hundred fifty leaves one thousand fifty.
<bookmark mark='blank'/>One thousand fifty add one thousand fifty is two thousand one hundred.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Add one thousand fifty once more. You reach three thousand one hundred fifty, the number already in the row.

beats.on_screen: the third row gets the board line 6,401 − 5,501 = 900; the blanks fill with 8,201 and 9,101
narration: <bookmark mark='gap'/>In the third row, take away five thousand five hundred one from six thousand four hundred one. That leaves nine hundred.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The rule is add nine hundred.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Seven thousand three hundred one add nine hundred is eight thousand two hundred one.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Add nine hundred again to reach nine thousand one hundred one.

<bookmark mark='add'/>Add the rule again and again.
<bookmark mark='land'/>You must land exactly on the last number that the row gives.
